summary: The 200 conditional-order limit is account-wide ('across all symbols', changelog 2025-12-29). The docs and gates.py say 'per symbol', and AGENTS demands dynamic discovery from exchangeInfo, which is impossible because the MAX_NUM_ALGO_ORDERS filter was removed.
expected: Keep the limit as a documented account-wide constant of 200. Count open algo orders across all symbols (GET /fapi/v1/openAlgoOrders without symbol, weight 40).
actual: EXEC_SPEC L153 says 'per symbol'. AGENTS says 'must be dynamic via exchangeInfo'. gates.py L27-35 says per symbol and plans to read MAX_NUM_ALGO_ORDERS (WR-06).
impact: A per-symbol count can pass the headroom gate while the account is at its cap. SL/TP placement then fails after the entry fills, and the position is unprotected. Hard to reach in V1 unless the account is shared.
evidence: Changelog 2025-12-29 (https://developers.binance.com/docs/derivatives/usds-margined-futures/change-log, read 2026-09-29): 'MAX_NUM_ALGO_ORDERS has been removed ... The conditional order limits is 200 across all symbols.' tests/fixtures/exchange_info_sample.json has no MAX_NUM_ALGO_ORDERS filter.
reproduction: Compare the EXEC_SPEC L153 wording with the changelog entry, and list the filterTypes in the fixture.
why_tests_miss: open_algo_count is an injected input; nothing checks the scope of the count.
recommendation: Fix the docs, INV-090 and AGENTS. Resolve AMB-032 as option (a). Drop the WR-06 MAX_NUM_ALGO_ORDERS plan. Code lanes should verify the count is account-wide.

summary: 'TradingView webhooks (HMAC-checked)' cannot be implemented: TradingView cannot sign requests or set custom headers.
expected: Authenticate with a secret in the URL path plus an allowlist of TradingView's 4 source IPs, acknowledge within 3 s, and dedupe payloads.
actual: AGENTS requires HMAC, and TRADINGVIEW.md s5 forbids secrets in the body, so the docs do not describe any working auth scheme.
impact: No live impact because no webhook is implemented. A future implementer could build something that cannot work, or fall back to an unauthenticated endpoint.
evidence: https://www.tradingview.com/support/solutions/43000529348-how-to-configure-webhook-alerts/ (read 2026-09-29): ports 80/443 only, 3 s timeout, IPs 52.89.214.238 / 34.212.75.30 / 54.218.53.128 / 52.32.178.7, 2FA required, no header or signing configuration.
recommendation: Rewrite AGENTS L77 and TRADINGVIEW.md s5 to specify URL-path secret + IP allowlist + fast ack + dedupe.
known_prior: INVARIANTS INV-112 flags this as QUESTIONABLE

summary: The docs do not mention the 2026-04-23 USD-M WebSocket base-URL split into /public, /market and /private. On legacy URLs, klines and user data silently stop.
expected: Klines are read via /market and user data via /private (SDK 17.4.0 routes this automatically). The stale-feed gate treats a connected but silent socket as stale.
actual: The docs are silent. The code uses the SDK, so the current risk is low.
impact: A regression (hand-rolled client or old SDK) would give a silent kline or user-data outage.
evidence: https://developers.binance.com/docs/derivatives/usds-margined-futures/websocket-market-streams/Important-WebSocket-Change-Notice (read 2026-09-29): 'Legacy URLs will remain available until 2026-04-23'; unmigrated connections get only /public. SDK websocket_streams.py L57 url_paths=['market','public','private'].
recommendation: Document the three bases in BINANCE.md. L5/L7 should verify the stale-feed gate catches a silent socket.

summary: The docs omit key algo-order semantics: there is no margin check before trigger; an order can be REJECTED or EXPIRED at trigger time; FINISHED means the child order was filled OR canceled, so it is not proof of an exit fill.
expected: The docs define algo status semantics: NEW is pending protection. REJECTED or EXPIRED after entry means the position is unprotected and must raise a HIGH alert or SAFE_MODE. An exit fill is confirmed from the child order (ai/aq, ORDER_TRADE_UPDATE).
actual: EXEC_SPEC s6 only requires the stop to 'exist and be active'. The code allow-lists NEW as active (manager.py L683-704); post-trigger handling was not traced.
impact: The position may be silently unprotected, or the exit may be mis-journaled (PnL, daily-loss state).
evidence: Changelog 2025-11-06: 'No margin check before the conditional order gets triggered'. Event-Algo-Order-Update statuses TRIGGERING / TRIGGERED / FINISHED / REJECTED / EXPIRED (search index, 2026-09-29). SDK algo_update_o.py fields rm, ai, aq, ap, act.
reproduction: Code lanes: grep fill_monitor and reconcile for how TRIGGERED, FINISHED, REJECTED and EXPIRED are interpreted.
recommendation: Add an algo status semantics subsection to EXEC_SPEC. Code lanes should verify post-trigger handling.

summary: fee_rate_entry=0.0002 assumes a maker fill, but the entry is a plain GTC LIMIT (manager.py L515), which fills as taker (0.0005) when it is marketable at submit time.
expected: Either use GTX (post-only) so the maker fee holds, or model the entry fee as taker or worst-case.
actual: Maker is assumed and GTC is sent. The VIP0 USDT-M values themselves (0.02%/0.05%) match secondary sources. The BNB discount is not modeled (conservative).
impact: The entry fee is understated by about 3 bps when the entry crosses the book, so realized risk is slightly above budget.
evidence: params comment '# 2 bps maker'; manager.py L515 'time_in_force': 'GTC'; error -5022 (GTX rejected) shows post-only exists; the official fee page did not render its table.
recommendation: Decide the entry TIF in the docs. Journal the m / n / N fields from fills and convert BNB commission to the quote asset. Phase 11 commissionRate.

summary: The quantization and constraint-snapshot docs ignore MARKET_LOT_SIZE (which applies to triggered *_MARKET exits with a quantity, such as TP1) and PERCENT_PRICE (a band on LIMIT prices). src has no reference to MARKET_LOT_SIZE.
expected: Snapshot and validate MARKET_LOT_SIZE and PERCENT_PRICE.
actual: Only LOT_SIZE, PRICE_FILTER and MIN_NOTIONAL are used.
impact: Latent. No effect for the live-5 at current capital (same step/min; maxQty far away).
evidence: Fixture: BTCUSDT LOT maxQty 1000 vs MARKET_LOT_SIZE maxQty 120; PERCENT_PRICE 1.05/0.95.
why_tests_miss: Values are identical for the live-5.
recommendation: Add both filters to the RISK s12 snapshot.

summary: The SDK types quantity/price/trigger_price as float and serializes them with str(float): values below 1e-4 become exponent strings (e.g. '1.234e-05') that Binance rejects. The docs do not define the Decimal-to-edge conversion.
expected: Document the rule: format tick-quantized Decimals as fixed-point strings before building floats, and never send exponent notation.
actual: Not documented. No impact on the live-5 (tick >= 0.0001, step >= 0.001).
evidence: binance_common/utils.py make_serializable: 'if isinstance(val, float): return str(val)'. Probe: str(float(Decimal('0.00001234'))) -> '1.234e-05'.
reproduction: venv python -c "from decimal import Decimal; print(str(float(Decimal('0.00001234'))))"
recommendation: Document the rule. L5 should verify the adapter conversion.
known_prior: The adapter docstring at binance_usdm.py L50 acknowledges the float boundary
